items_missed: Never got the customer's name — not once in 11.7 minutes. The transcript identifies the customer only as (512) 461-8099, and the rep never asked or used a name, which also zeroes out the Politeness name-use bullet.

No agenda roadmap. 'Do you happen to have around ten minutes or so, to talk about the details of your upcoming move?' gives the timeframe and asks permission, but never lays out the sequence (gather details, then walk through pricing), so it does not clear the agenda-opener bar.

Never checked Einstein's availability for the date. Customer floated Thursday October 1st as tentative; rep said 'we're happy to shift dates up or down or any which way' but never confirmed whether that date is actually open.
No stairs / floors question at either address — and the destination is a brand-new house the rep has never seen.

No special-considerations probe (long walk, narrow hallways, tight turns) on a move where every item is being carried roughly twenty paces across a property — walk distance is the single biggest time variable on this job and it went unasked.
No access probe — truck parking, driveway access, or approach at the new build.
No box count asked, even though packing was the central topic of the call.

Never asked the moving-stressors question. The customer handed him the cue twice: 45 years in the same house, never moved before, 'we're both in our seventies,' and 'we probably are going to have to get help from somewhere.' The rep answered the logistics and skipped the worry entirely.
No confirmation email mentioned. The only handoff explained was a text message with a walkthrough link, sent from an unfamiliar number — nothing in writing recapping the call or the plan.
No 'any other questions before I let you go?' — he closed with 'Then I will see you over there' and hung up.
Never gave hours or a way to reach him back, which matters more than usual here because he told the customer the incoming text would come from a different number than the one they were speaking on.

No Ecobox referral, which was squarely relevant — the customer is boxing a 2,200 sq ft house for a next-door move and explicitly did not want to buy-pack-unpack. Reusable box rental was the obvious answer to the problem the rep spent half the call describing.

Zero differentiators mentioned — No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, and the no-hidden-fees pitch were all absent. Not deducted (pricing is out of scope pre-walkthrough) but all four are free to say on an intake call.
Repetition cost real time — the 'boxing your dishes would waste your money' point was made three separate times at length before the rep moved on to scoping.
top_strength: He gave honest advice against his own commission and it built instant trust. Told a customer moving twenty paces next door that Einstein boxing her dishes would mean 'making a whole heck of a lot more trips than if it were in a box... we're kinda just to an extent just burning money at that point,' recommended she recruit family or friends for the small items, and volunteered that Einstein does not offer unpacking so buy-packing would just create work on the back end. He then closed the walkthrough cleanly and completely: framed it as 'similar to like a FaceTime,' checked she had a smartphone, asked whether she wanted to do it now or schedule it, and walked her through exactly what the text link would do and that it would ask for camera and mic access — no friction, done live on the call.
coaching_note: Scoring note first: this is a walkthrough scheduler (2,200 sq ft, routed to a virtual walkthrough), so Pricing, Clock, and Estimate were genuinely out of scope pre-walkthrough and are N/A-granted per the rubric — 37 of the 66 points are automatic. The 66 is not comparable to a full sales call score; the graded portion is 29 of 48. Highest-leverage fix: get the name in the first thirty seconds and use it. 'Before we dig in, who am I speaking with today?' costs four seconds and it cascaded — no name meant no name use, which cost the Politeness bullet and flattened the whole call into a transaction. Second: ask the worry question, especially here. Two people in their seventies, first move in 45 years, and they told you outright 'we probably are going to have to get help from somewhere.' The line is 'Is there anything you're particularly worried about with this move?' — and the answer would have set up your packing recommendation as reassurance instead of a policy explanation. Third: probe walk distance and access before the walkthrough, not during it. On a carry-it-across-the-yard move, walk distance is the estimate. Fourth: you made the boxing point three times — say it once, confirm with 'does that make sense?', and move on; you had four minutes of runway you could have spent on differentiators or an Ecobox referral, which was the obvious fit for a customer who wants boxes but not the buy-and-unpack cycle.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently pleasant with plenty of affirmations, but they are formulaic and repeated verbatim ('perfect, perfect,' 'absolutely, absolutely,' 'gotcha, gotcha'), he never learned or used the customer's name, and he let the clearest emotional cue in the call — 'we're both in our seventies... we probably are going to have to get help from somewhere' — pass with logistics rather than empathy.
